item.stem:
[Image: Right triangle on a coordinate plane]

A straight line l passes through the points A (1,−2) and B (3, 4).
Is the line l parallel with PQ?

Give a reason to support your answer.

descriptors: No, with correct work showing gradients are different, and leading to conclusion that l and PQ are not parallel.
No, with correct work leading to conclusion that l and PQ are not parallel using method other than showing gradients are different. For example, shows angle between the lines is not 0°
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.figure_description:
A Cartesian coordinate plane with horizontal axis x and vertical axis y intersecting at origin O. Tick marks are shown every unit on both axes. The x-axis is labeled at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and the y-axis is labeled at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. A right triangle is plotted in the first quadrant with vertices at point P, point Q, and a third vertex at the right angle:
- Point P is at coordinates (8, 1).
- A horizontal leg extends from P(8, 1) to (12, 1), with length labeled 4 beneath it.
- A vertical leg extends from (12, 1) upward to point Q at (12, 12), with length labeled 11 to its right.
- The hypotenuse connects point P to point Q.
item.calibration: Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
